the_ruling_verbatim: no we're going to need that before sharing it for real with the world. so time for a use case. In my vision, we have one or more 'top level agents' like you, with different specialties. Librarian is one. 'Igor' is one. [...] In my own household there's me, and Leah, my wife... And probably an igor, and perhaps other specialized agents as well that I can't imagine yet. so the problem of who owns what takes on a new dimension. now imagine a lab where the igor helps everybody in the lab. with all kinds of different things, some of them perhaps even requiring security clearences. and things like that change over time, so the igors would have to be adaptable.
no, the per owner database is a thing we do before things become even more complicated
now_the_spec_says: The per-owner database in the universal address (<owner db>.<table>.<leaf>) is foundational and is built now, with the address grammar and the link tuple, not deferred. Use case: a household or lab with several principals, one Igor serving all, clearances that change.
context: CC asked whether the per-owner segment of the universal address is a spec for db_domain's schema now or a horizon, then recommended the address grammar and link tuple now with the physical per-owner split as a later child. Akien answered with the vision (recorded whole in I-the-vision-that-guides-every-decision.md and through the idea door) and then ruled the order: the per-owner database comes now, before things become more complicated. Not marked RULED in his message. Both conforming files were restated in the same act; as_of pins the baseline at the commit before that restatement so verify measures the change.
